title: Signal Lattice Preflight Workbook
body:
Purpose:
This workbook is a compact, action-oriented KPI + readiness tracker built around a 'signal lattice' concept: each prelaunch signal (metric, qualitative check, dependency) is a node. Nodes are weighted and aggregated into an overall readiness index that feeds the launch cadence decision (go / hold / dial-back). Use this as the canonical daily tracker during the 2-week go/no-go window and as the seed for the launch runbook.

How to use (quick):
- Owners populate current values and short notes each morning.
- The lattice auto-scores (sheet formula): readiness_index = sum(weight_i * normalized_signal_i) / sum(weights).
- Decision thresholds: >= 0.82 = green (go-as-planned); 0.6-0.82 = amber (mitigate + re-evaluate); < 0.6 = red (pause or narrow scope).
- Primary escalation path: product-ops -> eng oncall -> SRE lead -> Head of Product.

Sheet layout (tabs recommended):
1) Signal Lattice (primary): columns = [signal_id, signal_name, category, owner, weight(0-1), baseline, target, current, normalized(0-1), delta, status_color, blocker_short, mitigation_action, last_update, link_to_artifact]
2) Sprint Traffic Plan: columns = [day, traffic_percent, canary_cohort, expected_qps, owner_oncall, notes]
3) Stakeholder Roster & Escalation: columns = [role, name, slack_handle, backup, escalation_window]
4) Lightweight Runbook Snippets: short commands + playbook step references.

Signal categories (examples):
- Performance: latency_p95_ms, mean_tokens_per_request, cold_start_time
- Cost & Economics: token_cost_per_1k, avg_inference_cost_usd, caching_hit_rate
- Reliability: error_rate_pct, uptime_30d, retry_rate
- Quality: eval_score_baseline, hallucination_rate_pct, regression_flag
- Ops Readiness: canary_users_enrolled, oncall_coverage_pct, infra_reserve_capacity_pct
- Compliance & Security: audit_log_ingest, kms_rotation_today, privacy_review_complete

Example rows (Signal Lattice tab) - fill in short text rows as morning snapshot:
- S001 | latency_p95_ms | Performance | Owen Brooks | 0.18 | 320 | <=300 | 340 | 0.44 | +40 | amber | investigate recent kernel change | rollback kernel patch + throttle non-critical jobs | 2025-03-04 | confluence:latency-investigation-03
- S010 | token_cost_per_1k | Cost | Lina Rodríguez | 0.12 | $2.10 | <=$1.80 | $2.05 | 0.15 | amber | cache miss rate spike | enable prefix cache refresh and temp-quant schedule | 2025-03-04 | JIRA:OPS-212
- S022 | eval_score_baseline | Quality | Jordan Patel | 0.2 | 0.86 | >=0.90 | 0.88 | 0.80 | green | n/a | add more eval prompts for edge cases | 2025-03-04 | github:evals/PR-119

Weighting guidance (how to set weights quickly):
- Performance/Quality/Reliability ~ 0.15-0.25 each for latency-sensitive product launches.
- Ops Readiness and Compliance ~ 0.08-0.15 depending on enterprise/regulatory surface.
- Cost can be lower weight for first wave but should be tracked.
- Sum(weights) should equal 1.0 for clarity.

Normalization examples (one-line):
- For metrics where lower is better (latency): normalized = clamp((target - current) / (target - baseline), 0, 1).
- For higher-is-better (cache_hit_rate): normalized = clamp((current - baseline) / (target - baseline), 0, 1).
- For boolean checks (privacy_review_complete): normalized = 1 if true else 0.

Sprint Traffic Plan (sample lane):
- Day 1 (canary): 0.1% traffic -> expected_qps 4 -> owner oncall: Owen Brooks -> notes: focus cohort: internal beta users, strict SLO monitoring
- Day 3 (expand): 1% traffic -> expected_qps 40 -> owner: Owen Brooks -> notes: enable autoscale headroom 20%
- Day 7 (ramp): 5% traffic -> expected_qps 200 -> owner: Lina Rodríguez -> notes: enable burst policy, monitor cost burn
- Day 14 (wide): 25% traffic -> expected_qps 1000 -> owner: Maya Chen -> notes: final go/no-go check at 12:00 UTC

Daily checklist (short, yes/no columns recommended in sheet):
- Are core SLOs within threshold?
- Any new production alerts in last 24h?
- Canary conversion and quality checks passed?
- Oncall coverage >= 2 engineers for 72h window?
- Backup / failback pipelines validated?
- Legal/compliance signoff present?

Escalation & decision play: (condensed)
- If readiness_index drops below 0.6: immediate oncall page and meeting within 30 min.
- If a single high-weight signal (weight >=0.15) flips to red: hold traffic expansion and remediate with rollback barn.
- Use silent rollback for model variant fallback when quality regressions exceed 2% absolute.

Operational snippets for runbook tab (copyable):
- throttle-noncritical: kubectl scale deployment worker --replicas=1 --context=prod-canary
- switch-model-variant: api call -> /v1/rollouts/fallback?model=redwood-v1-q4-lite
- drain-node: gcloud compute instances update --no-scheduler --name ${NODE}

Ownership shorthand (who does what):
- Product-ops (Maya) -> cadence, stakeholder comms, final go/no-go
- Serving runtime / SRE (Owen) -> latency, scaling, infra fallbacks
- Observability (Jordan) -> SLO dashboards, alert tuning, traces for regressions
- Finance / Cost (Lina) -> cost monitors, burst budget approvals

Notes on artifacts and hygiene: keep links short (confluence ids, jira keys). Each signal row should link to at least one artifact that explains the measurement method. Keep 'last_update' as ISO date. Avoid embedding long logs in the sheet; instead link to the log view or tracing PR.

Post-launch follow-ups (first 72h):
- Run the 'first-72h health audit' (sheet template attached as tab): owner collects per-signal post-launch drift and tags whether mitigation was temporary or permanent.
- Capture any model quality regressions in a dedicated 'evals' PR to avoid losing context.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Owners: populate signal rows for your domain by EOD today.
- Product-ops: finalize weight assignments by tomorrow morning based on product sensitivity score.
- Eng/SRE: create two quick rollback playbook gists and link them into Runbook Snippets.

Appendix - lightweight scoring examples (text):
- Example A: if latency p95 baseline 500ms -> target 300ms -> current 340ms -> normalized 0.8 -> contributes 0.144 to readiness when weight=0.18.
- Example B: a binary checklist (privacy_review_complete) with weight 0.10 -> if missing (0) then immediate floor on readiness by 0.10.

End of workbook.

Document history: created by Maya Chen to consolidate sprint-level preflight signals; intended as living sheet during rollout window; archived to confluence after +30 days post-launch with final lessons learned.
